significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a form-(iii) law—“repeating a claim within the context monotonically inflates” internally decoded belief as a dose-response independent of truth—and a form-(ii) mechanism in which a causally separable “familiarity/fluency” component can be ablated to restore truth-tracking. The phenomenon predicts belief changes across repetition counts, truth values, and paraphrases, while the mechanism would constrain how linear truth readouts such as those studied by Marks and Tegmark (2023) and Azaria and Mitchell (2023) should be interpreted when contextual familiarity varies. True and false outcomes are determinate: confirmation fixes a dose-response and causal decomposition, whereas refutation of the respective subclaims would rule out monotonic truth-independent inflation or a modular fluency mechanism, although rejection of the bundled hypothesis alone would be less informative. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on LLM beliefs would not merit this score; the additional measurable law and truth-versus-fluency decomposition make this substantially stronger than the median belief-direction hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users two explicit handles: “per-count belief/confidence dose-response slopes” as a diagnostic and an ablatable “familiarity/fluency” component that “restores truth-tracking” as an intervention. The diagnostic can screen contexts for repetition-driven contamination, and the ablation is ex ante because it can be applied before the model issues its truth judgment, giving auditors of echoed retrieval passages or repeated user assertions an action window. After model-specific re-extraction, the asserted monotonic, truth-independent dose-response still predicts what should be found rather than merely supplying a search procedure; the scope covers paraphrased and verbatim repetition, real and synthetic items, and LLMs broadly, though the claim expressly cautions that it “may not transfer to very large closed models.” The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the reach comes from the transferable dose relation and deployable ablation handle, not from the general importance of studying beliefs.
